new_task_1.title: Stop warning on attr.__version__ access
new_task_1.description: Version 23.2.0 changes the legacy module-metadata fallback so accessing `attr.__version__` or `attrs.__version__` still returns the installed package version but no longer emits a deprecation warning. Other deprecated metadata aliases remain warning-producing as before, and `__version_info__` continues to be exempt.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reading the public `__version__` attribute from the `attr` or `attrs` module returns the installed package version without triggering the deprecation warning that still applies to other legacy metadata aliases.

expectation.grounded: When module-level `__getattr__` handles `__version__`, it should resolve the version from package metadata and return it directly, skipping the deprecation warning path. The existing warning behavior for other legacy metadata attributes such as `__description__`, `__uri__`, or `__author__` should remain unchanged, and `__version_info__` should continue to return structured version information without warning.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to inspect the package version through the longstanding `__version__` attribute without noisy deprecation warnings, while the broader deprecation of other metadata shims stays in place.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to warning behavior for `__version__` lookups on the public modules. It must not change the returned version string, remove warnings from unrelated deprecated metadata aliases, or alter `__version_info__` handling.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should narrow the deprecation surface rather than redefining the legacy metadata API.

behavior: Accessing `attr.__version__` returns the installed attrs version string without emitting a deprecation warning.
Accessing `attrs.__version__` returns the installed attrs version string without emitting a deprecation warning.
Accessing `attr.__version_info__` or `attrs.__version_info__` continues to avoid warnings and returns version info as before.
Accessing other deprecated module metadata aliases continues to emit the existing deprecation warning.
acceptance_criteria: When code reads `attr.__version__`, it should receive the same version string reported by the installed package metadata and no deprecation warning should be recorded.
When code reads `attrs.__version__`, it should receive the same version string reported by the installed package metadata and no deprecation warning should be recorded.
When code reads another deprecated metadata alias such as `__description__`, the lookup should still emit a deprecation warning.
When code reads `__version_info__`, the lookup should continue to succeed without introducing a deprecation warning.

new_task_2.title: Correct min_len validation error wording
new_task_2.description: Version 23.2.0 corrects the public error message emitted by the `min_len` validator. Failed validations now report the minimum-length constraint using the correct `>=` operator instead of the incorrect `=>` text.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attr.validators.min_len()` reports failed minimum-length checks with an accurate, user-facing error message that describes the constraint as greater-than-or-equal-to the configured minimum length.

expectation.grounded: When a value shorter than the configured minimum length is validated, the raised `ValueError` message should read `Length of '<name>' must be >= <min>: <actual_len>` using the attribute name, configured minimum, and actual length. The validator's exception type and failure condition should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Validation failures should describe the actual rule being enforced, so users and tests see a correct minimum-length constraint instead of a typo.

constraints.grounded: Do not change when `min_len` raises, what exception type it raises, or how it calculates the observed length. Only the user-visible message text should be corrected.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve diagnostic accuracy without changing validator semantics.

behavior: If `min_len(n)` validates a value whose length is below `n`, it still raises `ValueError`.
The `ValueError` message now uses `>=` to describe the minimum-length requirement.
Successful validations and the validator's repr remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When `attr.validators.min_len(3)` validates a value of length 2 for an attribute named `x`, it should raise `ValueError` whose message states `Length of 'x' must be >= 3: 2`.
When a value meets or exceeds the configured minimum length, `min_len` should continue to succeed exactly as before.
The change should not alter the exception class or the validator's threshold logic.
